_comment: Description pairs whose TF-IDF similarity is above the threshold on purpose. Each entry names what tells the two apart in their descriptions; re-check that reason whenever either description changes. evals/descriptions/run.py reports an entry as stale once its pair scores more than 0.05 below the threshold.

pairs.reason: same fintech UI vocabulary (KYC, transactions, secure display) on different platforms: frontend-react says web/browser and excludes React Native; fintech-mobile says Flutter/iOS/Android apps and excludes mobile-number fields in web code

both dispatch subagents: dispatching-parallel-agents runs independent investigations or ad-hoc parallel tasks and points to build for the full-workflow build; build owns the build stage of a planned spec
consecutive AIDLC stages sharing aidlc verbs: build ends at `verified`; review starts when a spec reaches `verified` (or on a review request) and ends at `reviewed`
both write living docs: generate creates them when a service has none; upgrade promotes a verified or merged change into existing docs and closes the spec
chained on purpose for bug fixes (the router emits both): systematic-debugging finds the root cause, test-driven-development governs the failing test before the production edit

both deliver a branch (PR, merge, 'ship it'); they split by tier and each description points to the other: ship owns a reviewed full-workflow spec (ship.md, ship gate), finishing-a-development-branch owns fast-path or non-spec work. The router sends a bare 'ship it' to ship only, while finishing-a-development-branch still lists 'ship it' as a trigger phrase
